map.依据 GINA 近4周控制评估及 ACT(哮喘控制测试)量表，判断哮喘控制水平并: Based on GINA 4-week control assessment and the ACT (Asthma Control Test), it grades asthma control and guides step-up/step-down treatment
map.📖 查看「哮喘 GINA 控制水平评估器 使用指南」: 📖 View the Asthma GINA Control Level Assessor user guide
map.哮喘控制评估：GINA 近 4 周 4 项（日间症状 / 夜间憋醒 / 缓解药使: Asthma control: GINA 4 items over the past 4 weeks (daytime symptoms / night waking / reliever use / activity limitation) all 'no' means well controlled; ACT total = 5 items (1 to 5 each, max 25), >=20 well controlled, 16-19 not well controlled, <=15 very poorly controlled.
map.夜间因哮喘憋醒？: Waking at night due to asthma?
map.ACT 量表（5题，每题1–5分，满分25分）: ACT scale (5 questions, 1-5 points each, max 25)
map.1. 哮喘对工作/学习/家务妨碍程度: 1. How much asthma interferes with work/school/housework
map.3. 哮喘症状夜间憋醒频率: 3. Frequency of night waking from asthma symptoms
map.升级治疗，排查诱因与依从性: Step up treatment, review triggers and adherence
map.维持治疗，3–6月随访: Maintain treatment, follow up in 3-6 months
map.升级治疗，评估依从性与诱因: Step up treatment, assess adherence and triggers
map.提示：GINA推荐以哮喘控制为导向的治疗循环——评估控制、调整治疗、回顾应答。哮: Note: GINA recommends a control-based cycle - assess control, adjust treatment, review response. Acute exacerbations need separate severity assessment. Regular ICS-formoterol serves as both maintenance and reliever (MART). Clinical reference only.
map.GINA 四问全阴性→控制良好，维持当前阶梯，每 3–6 月复评。: GINA four questions all negative -> well controlled; maintain current step, review every 3-6 months.
map.ACT 5 题总分 20/25→部分控制，需升级治疗并随访。: ACT 5-item total 20/25 -> partly controlled; step up treatment and follow up.
map.GINA 为控制问卷、ACT 为症状+活动量表；联合更全面。: GINA is a control questionnaire, ACT covers symptoms plus activity; combining them is more comprehensive.
map.部分控制提示需升阶梯或更换吸入技术，2–4 周后复评。: Partial control means stepping up or correcting inhaler technique, then review in 2-4 weeks.
map.哮喘(GINA控制)评估器，依据近4周日间症状、夜间憋醒、缓解药使用、活动受限四: Asthma (GINA Control) Assessor grades asthma control across four dimensions over the past 4 weeks: daytime symptoms, night waking, reliever use and activity limitation (ACT/control level). A medical professional tool based on authoritative medical standards, for reference only.
